title: The Second Arrow
description: Ten minutes with the Buddha’s teaching on pain, and the resistance we add on top of it.

segments.say: Find a comfortable position, and close your eyes if you like.
Let the breath happen by itself for a moment.
The Buddha told a story. A person is struck by an arrow. It hurts.
Right after, they are struck by a second arrow, in the same place. Now it hurts twice.
The first arrow is pain. It comes with having a body and a life.
The second arrow is the one we shoot ourselves. Why me? This should not be happening. When will it stop?
The first cannot always be avoided. The second, often, can.
Let us look at this up close.
Look in the body for some discomfort. A tension, a small ache, a tired place.
If there is nothing in the body, bring to mind a light worry. Nothing too heavy.
Now just feel it. Where is it? How big? Is it warm, tight, throbbing?
This is the first arrow. Just sensation.
Now notice what comes with it. The bother about the bother.
Maybe an I don’t want this. A tightening around it. A story about what it means.
That is the second arrow. Notice that it is different from the first.
You do not need to pull out the second arrow. Just recognise it: ah, this is resistance.
And see what happens when you stop fighting the sensation, even a little.
Let the breath move around the pain, like water around a stone.
Often the pain stays. But the suffering on top of it gets smaller.
And when the second arrow comes back, and it will, just recognise it again.
Now let go of the focus on the sensation, and feel the whole body.
It is bigger than any discomfort inside it.
When you are ready, open your eyes.
